Subject: NovaHealth Dedicated Pool: post-call alignment & procurement touchpoints

Hi Claire — thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap from our call and the concrete next steps we discussed. I pulled the key pieces into bullets to keep things actionable.

Summary of current pain and goals
- Unpredictable latency during morning and end-of-day peaks (affects commit/lookup workflows).
- Need strict isolation for PII models (cannot share host tenancy with other customers).
- Target go-live: mid-Q2 (pilot in April, production by June).
- Cost goal: keep committed monthly spend under $XXk while meeting throughput/latency SLOs.

Technical targets we recorded
- Latency SLO: 95th percentile < 300ms for typical 256–512 token requests.
- Concurrency target: ~100 sustained concurrent inference requests per pool; ability to burst to ~250 for short windows.
- Model footprint: mixture of 13B and 34B variants; prefer quantized runtime for cost but need quality validation.
- Security: KMS integration, audit logs with 90-day retention, SOC2 evidence required during procurement.

Recommended Redwood configuration (initial proposal)
- Dedicated pool (reserved capacity) with isolated tenancy (no noisy neighbors).
- Suggested starting capacity: 4 x 80GB-equivalent GPUs with autoscale headroom + burst policy. We will validate sizing after we see a 48–72 hour traffic sample.
- Enable prefix/KV caching for low-latency hot routes.

Attachments sent
- novahealth_sla_draft_v1.pdf (SLA + security checklist)
- capacity_estimate_spreadsheet.xlsx (baseline sizing and cost estimate)

Agreed next steps (owners)
1) NovaHealth: share 48–72 hour traffic histogram and 7-day peak traces (Claire / engineering) — due Jan 20.
2) Redwood solutions: technical deep-dive to validate pool sizing and batching strategy (Jordan) — propose Jan 21 or 22.
3) Procurement: loop-in procurement contact and share MSA/draft terms (Tessa) — draft shared by Jan 19.
4) Security: complete initial answers to the SOC2/infosec checklist; we can provide audit artifacts upon NDA (Evelyn).

Claire — does this capture what we discussed? Any corrections or items to add? If the timing works, I’ll book the technical deep-dive for Jan 21 and drop the draft MSA into the Drive link below.

Thanks,
Tessa Morgan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Claire — quick technical note ahead of the deep-dive:
- Burst vs reserved billing: we support a reserved (committed) pool plus configured burst capacity that is billed at a higher rate when used. We can model capped burst windows (e.g., 10 minutes/hour) so you only pay for short spikes. Will include concrete numbers in the sizing spreadsheet.
- Sizing rationale: for the mix you described (13B / 34B quantized) and the target concurrency, the initial recommendation of 4 x 80GB-equivalent GPUs gives good headroom for caching and model variants. If you plan to keep 34B hot for the majority of traffic, we'll likely need a 6-GPU baseline; otherwise we can keep 4 GPUs and serve larger models via model variants with model-swap fallback.
- Ops: we’ll enable aggressive KV cache warming for the top 20% of routes and continuous batching parameters tuned to preserve the 95th < 300ms target.

To help size precisely, can you share an example 60-minute minute-by-minute request distribution (not just percentiles) and the breakdown between small/medium/long responses? If you prefer, we can accept a CSV upload to the Drive folder and I’ll run a quick simulation.

Jordan Blake
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
